subdivision.heading: Assessment of Costs by Assessment Officer

operative_text.controlling:
10.37(1)  A party entitled to payment of costs may obtain from an
assessment officer an appointment date for an assessment of costs.
(2)  If a party entitled to payment of costs makes the appointment,
that party must, 10 days or more before the appointment date,
(a) file a proposed bill of costs, and
(b) serve every party affected by the appointment with notice
of the appointment date in Form 45 and the proposed bill
of costs.
(3)  If any other party obtains an appointment date, that party must
(a) 20 days or more before the appointment date, serve notice
of the appointment date in Form 45 on every party
affected, and
(b) serve on the party entitled to payment of costs a request
that the entitled party prepare a proposed bill of costs.
(4)  The recipient of the request to prepare a proposed bill of costs
must do so as soon as practicable and file it and serve it on every
other party 10 days or more before the appointment date.
(5)  An assessment officer may vary a time period referred to in
this rule whether or not the period has passed.

BOOK_A.title: Appointment for Assessment
BOOK_A.commentary:
When the court awards costs between parties but does not specify their exact amount, the
procedure is as follows. The lawyer seeking costs draws up a bill of costs.¹
It is traditional to send
the draft bill of costs to the lawyer for the payor and ask him or her to agree as to the amount.
Often negotiation results. It is not necessary to wait a long time or reach agreement under R.
10.36(3). The payee can get a date from the assessment ofﬁcer for a hearing to approve or vary
the bill of costs, print up a formal appointment ﬁxing that day, have the Clerk sign and seal it, and
serve it on the payor’s lawyer. The other party has no right to object to large swathes of dates for
that hearing and so postpone the hearing unduly.²
Before an assessment of party-party costs, the payor need not give advance notice that he will
object that the proposed costs would exceed full indemnity.³

BOOK_C.title: Appointment for assessment

commentary.text:
The usual procedure is to contact the assessment officer’s office and obtain an appointment date, then file and serve the requisite materials setting the matter down.
Note the discretion of the assessment officer to vary time periods.
commentary.review_flag: The commentary 'General Principles' (two sentences, no citation): 'The usual procedure is to contact the assessment officer’s office and obtain an appointment date, then file and serve the requisite materials setting the matter down.' agrees with official 10.37(1)-(3) (obtain an appointment date; file and serve a proposed bill of costs and the notice in Form 45); 'Note the discretion of the assessment officer to vary time periods.' agrees with official 10.37(5). Neither sentence has an authority; Book A's note (the lawyer draws up the bill, sends it to the payor's lawyer for agreement, then obtains a date and has the Clerk sign and seal the appointment) covers the same procedure in other words.
